slides: Circles in questions. In the last lessons we learned the rules of the circle.

slides.say: Now we'll practice exam questions, basic ones and a bit more advanced ones, that use only these rules. Try each question yourself first, and then watch the solution.

Most circle questions come back to a few rules. First, all the radii of a circle are equal. So two radii and the chord between them make an isosceles triangle. Isosceles triangles hide inside almost every circle.
at: all the radii of a circle

slides.say: Second, a central angle is twice the inscribed angle on the same arc. A central angle of one hundred degrees gives an inscribed angle of fifty.
at: A central angle of one hundred

slides.say: And third, a radius to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent, so we get ninety degrees.

Notice that this radius wasn't in the drawing. We added it ourselves. A line we add like this is called a helper line, and many circle questions only open up after we draw one. So watch for them in the solutions. Let's start with a sample question. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next video.
